[alpha] is a degree-N(alpha) endomorphism, so x([alpha]P)=U(x)/V(x) is a rational function of degree N(alpha) in x (up to the usual sign/Kummer factor). An additive polynomial L of 2-degree k has degree 2^k. If L is not identically the rational function, the two agree on at most about N(alpha)+2^k points by Bezout/Schwartz-Zippel. They are identical only for alpha=+-tau^j on a Koblitz curve (x->x^2^j, the Frobenius, already the basis of the Frobenius-invariant factor bases and tau-Horner leads) or for degree-1 maps. So 'agreement negligible for alpha not a power of tau' is textbook, and the Drinfeld/EC gap is the known one: a Drinfeld module phi_a is an F_q-linear polynomial in tau by definition, while an elliptic curve endomorphism is a rational map of non-linear degree. Scope of this verdict: only the linearity-of-scalar-action hypothesis; does not close other Drinfeld analogies such as the factor base indexed by places in a tower, or the function-field IC mechanism.
